{{Quote|He doesn't like you."<br />"I'm sorry."<br />"I don't like you, either. You just watch yourself. We're wanted men. I have the death sentence on twelve systems."<br />"I'll be careful."<br />"You'll be dead!|Evazan and Luke Skywalker|<ref name="Episode 4">{{Film|IV}}</ref>}}
'''Cornelius Evazan''',<ref name="OFF">[[The Official Star Wars Fact File 51|''The Official Star Wars Fact File'' 51]]</ref> alias '''Roofoo'''<ref name="The Millennium Falcon Deal">{{SWRadio|The Millennium Falcon Deal}}</ref> and '''Doctor Cornelius''', also nicknamed '''Doctor Death''' or simply '''The Doctor''', was a notorious [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] outlaw and sociopath who was active during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. He considered himself a skilled [[Doctor/Legends|surgeon]], even though his patients were often maimed or killed after botched "operations." By the time of the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], his activities had earned him a death sentence in at least twelve systems.<ref name="Episode 4" />

==Biography==
===Early criminal career===
{{Quote|We're wanted men. I have the death sentence on twelve systems.|Evazan|audio=IHaveTheDeathSentenceOnTwelveSystems-ANH.flac|<ref name="Episode 4" />}}
Cornelius Evazan originally hailed from the [[Ecumenopolis/Legends|ecumenopolis]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Alsakan/Legends|Alsakan]] in the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]].<ref name="Star Wars Character Encyclopedia">''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia]]''</ref> No one knows if Evazan ever obtained a true medical degree. Nonetheless, he was remembered as a promising surgeon. His application to the [[Imperial Academy/Legends|Imperial Academy]] was rejected when his innate madness was revealed during an interview, and he was shipped off to the prison on [[Delrian/Legends|Delrian]]. Evazan escaped to the [[Hindasar system/Legends|Hindasar system]], where he established his own "practice" specializing in [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborging]] and inexpensive surgery.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 1">''[[Galaxy Guide 1: A New Hope]]''</ref> Once the medical and law-enforcement authorities caught up with him, he disappeared to another system, where he began his operations anew. He would repeat this process on several worlds, with occasional forays into [[Spice/Legends|spice]] [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggling]], [[Slavery/Legends|slaving]], [[Assassin/Legends|assassination]], and other crimes. He never stayed in one location too long, and his movement from planet to planet helped him gain more and more victims.<ref name="Evazan in the Databank" />

[[File:Cuttingedge.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Evazan at work, aided by Ponda Baba]]
His legacy of victims led him to be pursued by the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Jodo Kast]], who nearly caught up to him in the [[Corellian system/Legends|Corellian system]]. Thanks to the intervention of the [[Aqualish/Legends|Aqualish]] thug [[Ponda Baba/Legends|Ponda Baba]], Evazan escaped, but not before one of Jodo Kast's [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] shots caught him in the face. Evazan was scarred for life, but he and Baba formed a beneficial partnership.<ref name="Evazan in the Databank" />

===Partnership with Ponda Baba===
Evazan and Ponda Baba fled Corellia to hide out on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. It was there that he encountered a young [[Moisture farmer/Legends|moisture farmer]] named [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] in the [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Mos Eisley Cantina]]. They tried to bully the youth into a fight, but found themselves on the wrong side of [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi's]] lightsaber. The two of them fled the scene after Baba's arm was cut off.<ref name="Episode 4" /> Evazan did his best to replace his partner's arm with a cheap cybernetic replacement. The surgery was not a success, and Baba swore revenge, pursuing Evazan across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="Evazan in the Databank" />

===Project Starscream and the search for immortality===
{{Quote|Here lies Dr. Evazan. May he find the peace he did not give his patients.|Evazan's epitaph on [[Necropolis (Core Worlds)|Necropolis]]|<ref name="Galaxy of Fear: City of the Dead" />}}
Evazan returned to Tatooine and went into hiding, where he set up the [[Cutting Edge Clinic]] in [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]]. Under the name Doctor Cornelius, Evazan began operating on unsuspecting patients. He continued to specialize in cyborging and would occasionally use droid parts purchased from [[Jawa/Legends|Jawas]]. He was eventually forced to flee the planet and, soon after, he was confronted by his old partner, Ponda Baba. The two reconciled and set up base in a castle on [[Ando/Legends|Ando]], where Evazan made a new breakthrough. He came to the conclusion that it was the mind and not the body that was the key to immortality. He created a mind-transference machine, planning to transfer Ponda Baba's mind into a new body. He lured and trapped the Aqualish senator chosen to provide the body.<ref name="Doctor Death: The Tale of Dr. Evazan and Ponda Baba">{{StoryCite|story=Doctor Death: The Tale of Dr. Evazan and Ponda Baba|book=Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina}}</ref>

Evazan hoped to transfer his own mind into the body of a "perfect" young man he had captured earlier. Unfortunately for Evazan, the young man was actually a bounty hunter named [[Gurion Silizzar]] using a [[Multispectrum disguise suite|holoshroud]] to disguise himself. Gurion sought revenge because seven members of his family had been victims of Evazan's operations. Gurion forcibly escorted Evazan up to the castle's roof, where Gurion planned to kill the doctor. Evazan's pet [[meduza]], [[Rover (pet)|Rover]], saved Evazan's life by attacking Gurion, who then fell off the roof to his death. It was then that the Aqualish senator in Ponda Baba's body went up onto the roof and detonated a [[Thermal detonator/Legends|thermal detonator]]. Evazan fell off the roof moments before the explosion. Once again, Rover saved Evazan's life by sacrificing his own to cushion his master's fall.<ref name="Doctor Death: The Tale of Dr. Evazan and Ponda Baba" />

[[File:Galaxy_of_Fear.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Boba Fett blasting away Evazan's zombies]]
At an unknown time during the Galactic Civil War, Dr. Evazan conducted experiments on [[Peko-peko/Legends|peko-pekos]] from the planet [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], hoping to create invincible creatures that would act as his protectors and mounts. This experiment resulted in the creation of the [[toxic peko-peko]].<ref name="Card-SWGTCG-Toxic Peko-Peko Mount">{{SWGTCG|set=Agents of Deception|cardname=Toxic Peko-Peko Mount}}</ref>

Soon after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], Evazan went to work for [[Borborygmus Gog]], hoping to gain information from [[Project Starscream]] on bringing life to the dead. Evazan moved to Necropolis to work on bringing corpses to life as part of the project. However, during this time, [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] was pursuing Evazan. The bounty hunter caught up to Evazan on the planet [[Necropolis (Core Worlds)|Necropolis]] and executed the mad doctor by shooting him with a single blaster bolt while he was holding [[Zak Arranda/Legends|Zak Arranda]] hostage.<ref name="Galaxy of Fear: City of the Dead" />

[[Pylum]] required that Fett leave Evazan's body behind, in hopes of holding off the [[Curse of Sycorax]], and Fett agreed, but held them all responsible if he never collected the full bounty. Unknown to them all, Evazan had injected himself with a megadose of his own reanimation serum, and he eventually returned to life. However, the serum only worked well on recently dead bodies. The longer the body stayed dead before being injected, the less likely it was to survive reanimation. Evazan nearly completed his work, but was stopped by the zombie [[Kairn]]. Evazan tried to eliminate Hoole, Zak, and [[Tash Arranda/Legends|Tash Arranda]], but Kairn refused to see his friends killed. He used a vial of the anti-serum created by [[DV-9]] to kill the zombie army Evazan had created, by splashing it over them, but was killed himself when some of it splashed onto him. Fett then took the vial from Kairn's hand and threw it at Evazan, and it shattered as it hit the evil doctor, with the liqud splashing across his face. Evazan then screamed and dropped to his knees before twitching and falling face-first to the floor, seemingly dead as a result of coming into contact with the liquid.<ref name="Galaxy of Fear: City of the Dead" />

However, Evazan seemingly cheated death yet again. As late as [[9 ABY/Legends|9 ABY]], the doctor was reportedly still at large. Baba also survived, in the body of the senator, and again sought revenge against Evazan.<ref name="Evazan in the Databank" />

==Personality and traits==
Evazan was a ruthless scientist who would stop a stop at nothing to achieve his goals. He showed no compassion for sentient life, even using the human child, Zak Arranda, as a human shield against Boba Fett, as he knew that Fett would not want to kill a child. He also murdered the human boy Kairn, again showing that he was willing to sacrifice anyone, even children, to achieve his goals. He treated his test subjects as nothing more than objects, describing the horrific experiments he wanted to perform on them in a cold and uncaring voice. And he displayed a strong sadistic streak, laughing at Tash Arranda and mocking her when she believed he had killed her brother, instead blaming her for his death. However, he also possessed a sense of fairness, told his test subjects everything about the experiements he subjected them to, as he believed it was fair for them to know, since they helped him achieve his success. He smiled as he told them what would happen, showing no sympathy whatsoever at the terror they felt. And he mocked his victims for attempting to flee before he could carry out his experiments, telling them that they could not leave just as the fun was about to begin, further showcasing his sadistic nature. And he willingly placed the Shi'ido Hoole in danger simply so that Hoole could fight his experiments, as he wanted to prove how strong his zombies were, not caring that he placed Hoole's life in danger in the process. And he seemed to have a strong dislike towards children in general, calling them brats.<ref name="Galaxy of Fear: City of the Dead" />

He was also a narcissist, stating that he possessed 'great scientific genius' and triumphantly bragging about his achievements. However, despite his inflated sense of self-worth, he also acknowledged his own weak points. He openly stated that he needed to practice his bedside manner, which people had told him was his weak point. And he also knew that he could not permanently hide from Boba Fett forever, due to Fett's superior tracking skills, so he allowed himself to be killed by Fett and later reanimated instead of constantly trying to evade the bounty hunter.<ref name="Galaxy of Fear: City of the Dead" />

Despite his high intelligence, Evazan also became careless when he believed that he had reached his goals and defeated his enemies, even falling for obvious tricks, as he loudly bragged that he had one when he believed that he had outsmarted Boba Fett, failing to realize that he was talking to an empty suit of armor, and that Fett was actually stalking him from behind, allowing Fett to shoot him with his blaster. He also became irate when his experiments disobeyed him, angrily yelling at the zombified Kairn when he spoke without permission and when he defied orders, and later loudly screaming obscenities when Kairn continued to betray him by helping his enemies, showing that he lost his temper and his composure when things went wrong.<ref name="Galaxy of Fear: City of the Dead" />

He was proud of his infamous reputation, as he openly bragged about having the death penalty on twelve systems. And he was prone to becoming rowdy and starting arguments, especially when under the influence of alcohol.<ref name="Episode 4" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:DrEvazan.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Dr. Evazan first appeared in ''A New Hope''.]]
[[Alfie Curtis]] played Dr. Evazan in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''A New Hope'']].<ref name="Evazan in the Databank" />

Evazan first appeared in the [[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|novelization]] of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''A New Hope'']], ghostwritten by [[Alan Dean Foster]] and published in [[1976]], half a year before the film. Evazan was unnamed and described as a short Human. In his scene, he was accompanied by a many-eyed and a rodent-like alien&mdash;early incarnations of Ponda Baba and [[Kabe/Legends|Kabe]]&mdash;when they insulted Luke Skywalker. In this version, Obi-Wan Kenobi sliced Evazan's hand and cut Kabe and Baba in half. In the Revised Fourth Draft of the screenplay&mdash;calling Evazan and Baba "Human" and "Creature"&mdash;the scene was about the same. In the final film, Kabe did not accompany Evazan, and Obi-Wan Kenobi dealt less drastically with the outlaws.

In ''[[Robot Chicken: Star Wars]]'', Evazan is portrayed as a compulsive joker who does not know when to keep his mouth shut—which leads to the loss of Ponda Baba's arm when he jokes that he and Ponda are wanted men.

During the 2012 Super Bowl, Evazan appeared shortly after the Volkswagen commercial of a dog exercising and chasing a car, mocking "The Force" ad from the previous year (where a child dressed up as Darth Vader attempts to use [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to start a Passat, only to be stunned when his father engages the remote ignition). He ends up nearly strangled by Darth Vader, who was present among the patrons and apparently overheard Evazan, prompting Evazan to apologize.<ref name="Super Bowl 2012">{{SWArchive|url=news/volkswagen_cantina_super_bowl_ad.html|text=Volkswagen Returns to the ''Star Wars'' Cantina}}</ref>
